en: Udāna 4.6 Piṇḍola Sutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja was sitting not far from the Blessed One,

having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and— being a forest-dweller, an almsfood eater, a rag-robe wearer, a wearer of the three robes, one of few desires— maintained mindfulness directed to the body.
Contented, secluded, unattached, energetic, a proponent of the ascetic practices (*dhuta*), and devoted to higher mental training—
the Blessed One saw the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise and set his body erect:
a forest-dweller, an alms-food eater, a wearer of rag-robes, one who possesses only three robes, few in desires, and contented.
One who is secluded, unattached, energetic, a proponent of the ascetic practices (dhuta), and devoted to higher consciousness.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
